# Design advanced spaceships

**Every new spaceship uses SNOT by default. Start with the [Halcyon interceptor](../../examples/snot/halcyon/README.md) as the default construction and visual-quality reference.** Its supported core, sideways hull skins, axial intakes and exhausts, smooth contours and thin wings establish the approach. Use SNOT for substantial exterior surfaces and give each surface a real attachment. An upright internal core is appropriate; the exterior should have deliberately shaped panels and a coherent silhouette.

Apply this workflow to starfighters, freighters, shuttles and capital ships, including Star Wars subjects. Adapt Halcyon's construction principles to the requested scale and identity. Use the [spaceship atlas](../../examples/spaceship-atlas/README.md) for supporting silhouette, cockpit, engine, wing and armour studies. Keep source authorship when copying a construction.

```sh
./ldraw-agent spaceship list
./ldraw-agent spaceship details
./ldraw-agent examples --family spaceship
./ldraw-agent examples --family spaceship --details
./ldraw-agent spaceship brief starfighter --output output/my-ship-brief.json
```

`brief` also accepts `freighter` and `capital-ship`. It supplies design roles, module suggestions, part-search prompts and a review checklist. Complete its scale, dimensions, pose and attachment decisions before building; it is a brief, not a generated model.

## Establish identity and scale

Decide whether the model is minifigure scale, a larger display model or microscale. Choose two or three defining masses before adding small details: an X-shaped wing arrangement, a long engine pair, a broad asymmetric cargo hull, or a wedge with a raised bridge. For a named fictional ship, study the specific variant and retain its defining proportions.

For new designs use X for width, -Z for forward and negative Y for up. Choose a hull or display-stand datum explicitly; spacecraft do not inherit a car's wheelbase and road plane. Imported source axes may differ. Measure the source before rotating or positioning it, and use proper rotations rather than mirrored or stretched parts.

| Family | Main construction decisions | Visual priorities |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Starfighter/interceptor | Central spine, wing roots, cockpit, nacelles and landing/display attachments | Nose/cockpit balance, thin wing edges, engine spacing and a distinct front silhouette |
| Freighter/shuttle | Cargo frame, access corridor, hull panels, ramp, cockpit and landing supports | Hull mass, deliberate asymmetry, readable loading access and restrained weathering accents |
| Capital ship | Internal truss, lower hull, paired upper panels, bridge, trenches and engine block | Large clean outline, layered silhouette, recessed detail and consistent miniature scale |

## Study constructions and choose real parts

Use Jev only after its availability check; use explicit FTS when unavailable. Search separately for whole-ship proportions and each construction role. Do not restrict useful source parts to the same theme. Spacecraft often combine System skins with Technic frames; `--construction all` helps discover both.

```sh
./ldraw-agent discover search models 'a detailed Star Wars starfighter with wing and engine submodels' \
  --construction all --min-parts 300 --max-parts 2500 --limit 5
./ldraw-agent discover search submodels 'a spaceship engine nacelle with a cylindrical shell and exhaust' \
  --construction all --max-parts 180 --limit 5
```

Inspect dedicated canopies and windscreens with their mating rims, printed instrument tiles, seats and control sticks, matched wedge plates, curved slopes, brackets, hinge halves, cylinders, dishes, cones, grilles, bars and clips. Preserve embedded custom definitions where the source needs them. Do not invent a part ID or replace all these distinctive forms with rectangular slabs.

Use [build pages](build-manuals.md) when layers or hidden interfaces are hard to read. The atlas includes manuals for an X-wing nacelle, an enclosed canopy cockpit, a UCS Y-wing armour panel and a Millennium Falcon service cluster. Its larger wing study includes source sections that can be expanded into manuals when needed.

The [6208 B-Wing SNOT study](../../examples/snot/b-wing-6208/README.md) supplies a complementary introduction with 22 inspected views and two exposed-core selections. It uses the supplied 6208 source, distinct from the atlas's 75050 B-Wing. Geometry and flexible-part verification are deferred for that learning study.

Halcyon's generator, exposed-core images, module views and visual review show the complete workflow. Read its [attachment map](../../examples/snot/halcyon/README.md#3-module-topology) before adapting the local frames and panel mounts.

## Build surfaces in their own local grids

The 6208 construction shows four useful ways to attach a spaceship's outer surfaces:

| Surface role | Source example | Design lesson |
|---|---|---|
| Fixed perpendicular details | `Center Front`: opposing `44728` brackets, a `2436a` bracket and `52107` side-stud bricks | Establish the stud faces before adding tiles, fins and slopes |
| Curved skin around a Technic core | `Center Side 2`: axle connectors, `4032a` round plates and opposing plate skins | Separate the internal attachment system from the visible surface grid |
| Angled armour | `Center Front`: `3937`/`6134` hinge pairs | Give oblique panels their own attachment and local plane |
| Large wing module | `Center Side 1` carrier and the three wing sections | Build a thin local wing with a defined root, then orient the whole module in its parent |

Choose the interface that serves the surface's role. A rotated module can contain mostly ordinary upright stacks in its own frame. Keep that frame readable, and distinguish its local up direction from the complete ship's pose. The cockpit and its support arm are a useful example of this separation.

For visual variety, combine a few broad wing or hull shapes with small repeated engine and tip details. The 6208 exhaust uses four round-brick/dish nozzle stacks; its cockpit is shaped around a dedicated transparent canopy. Source prose can misdescribe those parts, so read the actual inventory and images. Its sections each contain one construction state: selected-part cutaways reveal layers, but are not source build steps.

## Build from the frame outward

Reserve the cockpit, cargo volume, engine envelopes and attachment space first. Separate the internal spine/truss, cockpit tub, nose, wing roots, wings, engines, hull panels, service details and landing/display supports. Record each module's local origin, bounds, mounting parts and dependencies.

Long wings and cantilevered engines need a bonded plate stack or a braced frame. Do not place a wing or pod in space merely because its bounding box touches the hull. Keep a bare-frame or root close-up to inspect the real attachment. Use the [Technic workflow](technic.md) for fixed supports and the [mechanism workflow](mechanisms.md) for actual folding wings, ramps or retracting gear. Analytical mechanism verification remains deferred; a static hinge pose does not demonstrate motion.

Copy the default design as an editable starting point:

```sh
./ldraw-agent spaceship export halcyon --outdir output/my-starship
./ldraw-agent build output/my-starship/halcyon.plan.json \
  --output output/my-starship/my-starship.mpd
```

For Halcyon, edit its generator and rebuild the plan. Other atlas exports supply a placement plan and attributed `source.mpd`; edit the placement plan to position the whole module and the source for internal changes. An origin frame is not a promised connector. Check new interfaces and fixed supports separately. Export remains blocked for inspiration entries with unresolved source errors. Whole-model source studies can contain minifigures, stands or accessories; inspect their section lists.

## Make the design attractive

Keep the primary hull colour dominant and use smaller roles

# Halcyon: an original SNOT interceptor

**This is the default model to follow for spaceship construction and visual quality. All new spaceships use SNOT by default.** Adapt its core-and-skin construction to the requested ship's silhouette and scale. Copy the editable design with `./ldraw-agent spaceship export halcyon --outdir output/my-ship`.

**A studs-up core supplies stud faces in five directions; the side, front and rear surfaces are modules built upright in their own frames and turned onto those faces.** The parrot, cat, F40 and B-Wing are prepared from existing models. The Halcyon is the first original design in this folder to use those lessons.

![Halcyon on its stand](halcyon.png)

| Study | Pieces | Editable source | Ready MPD |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Complete ship, stand and 16 modules | 195 | [generate.py](generate.py) → [halcyon.plan.json](halcyon.plan.json) | [halcyon.mpd](halcyon.mpd) |

```sh
.venv/bin/python examples/snot/halcyon/generate.py
./ldraw-agent review examples/snot/halcyon/halcyon.plan.json --outdir output/snot-halcyon-review \
  --contacts all --views home front back left right top bottom
./ldraw-agent manual prepare output/snot-halcyon-review/model.mpd --section halcyon-hull.ldr \
  --outdir output/snot-halcyon-steps/halcyon-hull --views home back
```

The generator writes an ordinary plan for the existing builder; it adds no format or library code. Ship axes follow the [spaceship guide](../../../docs/agent/spaceships.md): X is width (starboard +X), -Z is forward, -Y is up. Y=0 is the keel underside. The ship measures 584 × 480 × 140 LDU (about 29 × 24 × 7 studs) without its stand.

![Front, back, starboard side and top](views.png)

## 1. Build the core first and expose its stud faces

The hull is a plain studs-up stack. Its one brick course uses fifteen `30414` bricks (1 × 4, side studs on one face), each yawed so its studs face the module it carries. Hull step 5 shows them before anything covers them:

![Side-stud course: ±X faces for flanks and pod stripes (left); twelve aft studs for nozzles and aft cap (right)](core.png)

| Layer | Top Y | Contents |
|---|---:|---|
| K1–K4 | -8, -16, -24, -32 | Keel plates. K1/K3 and K2/K4 use different seams; K2/K4 bridge the core/pod joint at x=±40 |
| K5 | -40 | Only under the nose cap |
| Side-stud course | -56 | `30414` side studs at Y=-46; plain bricks elsewhere |
| Deck | -64 | Tiles, cockpit floor plate, curved pod tops |

All side studs sit at Y=-46, 10 LDU below the course top. This one height lets the flank stripe and pod stripes line up. Unrotated, `30414` has its studs on the -Z face, so yaw selects the direction: 0° faces forward, 180° faces aft, -90° faces +X and 90° faces -X.

## 2. Build each skin upright, then turn it onto a face

Each sideways module is authored as an ordinary upright stack, so plates still sit on studs and tiles still cover them. The root then rotates the whole module so its local up (-Y) faces the stud face:

![Modules in their own frames: flank and pod stripe (flat panels), nose (ship frame), intake, exhaust and cannon (stacks along their own axis)](modules.png)

| Module | Local up becomes | Seated on | Contacts |
|---|---|---|---:|
| `halcyon-flank-s/p` | ±X | three `30414` per side, x=±40 | 12 each |
| `halcyon-pod-panel-s/p` | ±X | two `30414` per pod, x=±120 | 8 each |
| `halcyon-intake` (×2) | -Z | one `30414` per pod front, Z=40 | 4 each |
| `halcyon-exhaust` (×2) | +Z | one `30414` per pod rear, Z=240 | 4 each |
| `halcyon-aft-cap` | +Z | centre `30414`, Z=240 | 4 |
| `halcyon-cannon` (×2) | -Z | one `87087` on each wing root | 1 each |

The root computes each origin as `stud - R * socket`, as in the [SNOT guide](../../../docs/agent/snot.md#start-from-a-real-connection). For the starboard exhaust, `R = [[1,0,0],[0,0,1],[0,-1,0]]` sends local up to +Z. The ring's socket `[10,8,-10]` becomes `[10,-10,-8]`. Seated on the stud at `[90,-46,240]`, it gives the origin `[80,-36,248]`. The intake, exhaust and cannon are rotationally symmetric about their own axes, so each is one section placed twice by translation.

The port flank uses the same parts as the starboard one, but a different proper rotation. That rotation sends local Z to the opposite world direction, so the port section puts its accent row at local Z=-10 instead of +10. Nothing is mirrored.

## 3. Module topology

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Stand[Stand: round column] -->|4 studs into K1 underside| Hull
    Hull[Hull core: K1-K4, side-stud course, deck]
    Hull -->|12 side studs per side, x=±40| Flanks[Flank panels ×2]
    Hull -->|8 side studs per pod, x=±120| Pods[Pod stripes ×2]
    Hull -->|4 forward studs per pod, Z=40| Intakes[Intakes ×2]
    Hull -->|4 aft studs per pod, Z=240| Exhausts[Exhausts ×2]
    Hull -->|4 aft studs, Z=240| Cap[Aft cap]
    Hull -->|4 floor studs, x=±10| Canopy[30384 canopy]
    Hull ===|wedge pairs overlap one hull row per keel layer| Nose[Nose: stepped wedges + 47753]
    Hull ===|inner column between K1 
... [truncated: 8180 characters total; continue at offset 5000]

The reference is a small Technic-core fighter, about 500 × 90 LDU. It has a black and dark-bluish-grey scheme, two yellow accent studs and several kinds of sideways attachment.

- **Core:** `3703` and `3701` Technic bricks with pins.
- **Skins:** `30414` side-stud bricks carry the hull surfaces.
- **Wings:** pairs of `41769`/`41770` wings and `43722`/`43723` wings, with `2654` dishes as thrusters.
- **Rear and nose:** a `43713` wedge at the rear and a `50745` mudguard at the nose.

I haven't built anything yet. This is the plan I propose.

## Concept
**"Kestrel-class strike skiff"** is an original ship in the same visual language. It is a long, slim fighter with a narrow nose, swept paired wings and a thruster cluster at the rear. It is not a copy of the Naganata. I'd make it larger and more detailed, about 700 × 520 × 120 LDU (roughly 35 × 26 studs).

## Palette
- **Dominant:** dark bluish grey (72).
- **Secondary:** black (0) for the panel breaks, the thruster dishes and the underside.
- **Accents:** yellow (14) for the intake studs, plus small trans-blue or trans-orange on the thrusters. I'll check which colours the parts actually come in.

## Construction, following Halcyon
1. **Core:**
   - A studs-up Technic brick spine (`3703`/`3701`) pinned with `4459`, as in the reference.
   - A course of `30414` side-stud bricks, yawed so their studs face ±X, forward and aft.
   - Plate layers above and below to tie the pieces together.
2. **Modules:** each is built upright in its own section and rotated onto a stud face using `stud − R·socket`.
   - Flank panels ×2, built from plates and tiles.
   - Wing modules ×2, thin and swept, using the `41769`/`41770` and `43722`/`43723` wings on a bonded plate root.
   - Thruster cluster, using `2654` dishes and round bricks on an aft `30414` face.
   - Nose cone, with slopes and a curved mudguard or wedge.
   - Cockpit canopy on a floor plate.
   - Two wing-root cannons on `87087` bricks.
3. **Display stand:** a small stand so the ship is not left floating.

## Workflow
1. **Brief and notes:** write `output/kestrel/brief.md`, then check Jev availability and record the result in `output/NOTES.md`.
2. **Part inspection:** inspect the part origins and connectors with `./ldraw-agent part` for:
   - `30414`
   - `87087`
   - `41769`
   - `41770`
   - `43713`
   - `2654`
   - `3062b`
   - the canopy
3. **Generator:** write `output/kestrel/generate.py`, which emits `kestrel.plan.json`.
4. **Build and review:**
   - Build the model.
   - Run `review --contacts all`, with the views home, front, back, left, right, top and bottom.
   - Open each preview.
   - Check silhouette, wing roots, bare sides and the thruster.
   - Fix problems in the generator, rebuild and re-render.
5. **Delivery:**
   - Publish the model.
   - Report the placement count, the checks that passed and any limitations. Physical validity stays "not proven".

"""Halcyon: an original SNOT interceptor, generated as an ordinary JSON plan.

Run from the repository root:

    .venv/bin/python examples/snot/halcyon/generate.py
    ./ldraw-agent review examples/snot/halcyon/halcyon.plan.json --outdir output/snot-halcyon-review

Ship axes: X is width (starboard +X), -Z is forward, -Y is up. Y=0 is the keel underside and the
origin is the keel centre at the wing roots. Each module has its own local frame; the root places it.
Every sideways part is seated with origin = stud - R * socket, using inspected connector positions.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
for parent in HERE.parents:
    if (parent / 'ldraw_tools').is_dir():
        sys.path.insert(0, str(parent))
        break

from ldraw_tools.builder import rotation  # noqa: E402

AUTHOR = 'Halcyon generator (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5) for anteloc'

# Palette roles (LDraw codes)
HULL, PANEL, FRAME, ACCENT, BLACK = 15, 71, 72, 321, 0   # white, light/dark bluish grey, dark azure, black
GLASS, GLOW = 40, 57                               # trans-black canopy, trans-orange

# Hull layers: plate/brick tops (part origins), keel underside at Y=0.
K1, K2, K3, K4, K5 = -8, -16, -24, -32, -40         # keel plates; K5 exists only under the nose cap
COURSE = -56                                       # side-stud brick course; its side studs are at Y=-46
SIDE_STUD_Y = COURSE + 10
DECK = -64                                         # deck tiles and slopes

# Each keel layer's hull plates start at NOSE_STEP[layer]; that layer's nose wedge pair fills the 80 LDU ahead.
NOSE_STEP = {K1: -140, K2: -160, K3: -180, K4: -200, K5: -220}


def Ry(degrees):
    return np.array(rotation('y', degrees).rows, float)


def orient(up, along):
    """Proper rotation sending the part's local up (-Y) to `up` and its local +X to `along`."""
    x = np.array(along, float)
    y = -np.array(up, float)
    r = np.column_stack([x, y, np.cross(x, y)])
    assert np.allclose(r.T @ r, np.eye(3)) and np.isclose(np.linalg.det(r), 1)
    return r


def seat(r, socket, stud):
    """Part origin placing its local `socket` exactly on the target `stud` base."""
    return np.array(stud, float) - r @ np.array(socket, float)


def clean(v):
    out = float(round(float(v), 9))
    return 0.0 if out == 0 else out


class Section:
    def __init__(self, name, description):
        self.name, self.description, self.steps = name, description, []

    def step(self):
        self.steps.append([])
        return self

    def add(self, id, ref, colour, at, r=None, purpose=None):
        ref = ref if ref.endswith(('.dat', '.ldr')) else ref + '.dat'
        entry = dict(id=id, ref=ref, colour=colour, at=[clean(v) for v in at])
        if r is not None and not np.allclose(r, np.eye(3)):
            entry['matrix'] = [[clean(v) for v in row] for row in np.asarray(r)]
        if purpose:
            entry['purpose'] = purpose
        if not self.steps:
            self.step()
        self.steps[-1].append(entry)
        return entry

    def box(self, id, ref, colour, x0, x1, z0, z1, top, purpose=None):
        """Upright rectangular part covering [x0,x1] x [z0,z1] with its origin (body top) at `top`."""
        nx, nz = DIMS[ref]
        w, d = (x1 - x0) / 20, (z1 - z0) / 20
        if (w, d) == (nx, nz):
            r = None
        elif (w, d) == (nz, nx):
            r = Ry(90)
        else:
            raise ValueError(f'{id}: {ref} is {nx}x{nz}, not {w}x{d}')
        return self.add(id, ref, colour, [(x0 + x1) / 2, top, (z0 + z1) / 2], r, purpose)

    def plan(self):
        return dict(name=self.name, description=self.description, steps=[s for s in self.steps if s])


# x_studs (local X) and z_studs (local Z) of the upright rectangular parts used with Section.box.
DIMS = {
    '3022': (2, 2), '3710': (4, 1), '3034': (8, 2), '3032': (6, 4), '3035': (8, 4), '3036': (8, 6),
    '3030': (10, 4), '3001': (4, 2), '3010': (4, 1), '3008': (8, 1), '3007': (8, 2),
    '3068b': (2, 2), '3069b': (2, 1), '63864': (3, 1), '2431': (4, 1), '6636': (6, 1), '87079': (4, 2),
    '2412b': (2, 1),
}


def side_stud_brick(sec, id, ref, colour, face, centre, top):
    """Place 30414 so its side studs face `face` (+-X or +-Z); `centre` is the brick centre (x, z).

    Unrotated, 30414's four side studs sit on its -Z face (Z=-10), 10 LDU below its top.
    """
    yaw = {(0, 0, -1): 0, (1, 0, 0): -90, (0, 0, 1): 180, (-1, 0, 0): 90}[tuple(face)]
    return sec.add(id, ref, colour, [centre[0], top, centre[1]], Ry(yaw), 'studs face ' + str(face))


# --- modules --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

SIDES = (('s', 1), ('p', -1))


def xs(sx, a, b):
    """Sorted x interval for a starboard interval [a, b] mirrored by side sign sx."""
    return tuple(sorted((a * sx, b * sx)))


def hull():
    """Keel, side-stud course and deck: a studs-up core exposing stud faces to +-X, -Z and +Z.

    The forward hull (z=-220..40) is four studs wide; the engine pods widen it to twelve studs
    from z=40 to 240. K1/K3 and K2/K4 use different seams, and K2/K4 bridge the core/pod seams at
    x=+-40. Each keel layer starts at NOSE_STEP, where that layer's nose wedge pair ends.
    """
    s = Section('halcyon-hull.ldr', 'Halcyon hull core and engine pods: four keel plates, side-stud course, deck')
    for name, y, fwd in (('k1', K1, '3034'), ('k3', K3, '3030')):
        s.step()
        half = 20 if y == K1 else 40                # K1 leaves room for the two strakes
        s.box(f'{name}-fwd', fwd, FRAME, -half, half, NOSE_STEP[y], 20, y)
        s.box(f'{name}-waist', '3710', FRAME, -40, 40, 20, 40, y)
        s.box(f'{name}-aft', '3030', FRAME, -40, 40, 40, 240, y)
        for side, sx in SIDES:
            s.box(f'{name}-pod-{side}', '3030', FRAME, *xs(sx, 40, 120), 40, 240, y)
        if name == 'k1':
            s.step()
            k2_k4(s, 'k2', K2)
    s.step()
    k2_k4(s, 'k4', K4)
    for side, sx in SIDES:
        s.box(f'k4-pod-out-{side}', '3034', FRAME, *xs(sx, 80, 120), 40, 200, K4)
        s.box(f'k4-pod-tail-{side}', '3022', FRAME, *xs(sx, 80, 120), 200, 240, K4)

    s.step()  # Side-stud course: flank, intake, exhaust and tail stud faces
    for side, sx in SIDES:
        face = (sx, 0, 0)
        for i, z in enumerate((-180, -100, -20)):
            side_stud_brick(s, f'flank-mount-{i}-{side}', '30414', HULL, face, (30 * sx, z), COURSE)
        side_stud_brick(s, f'intake-mount-{side}', '30414', FRAME, (0, 0, -1), (80 * sx, 50), COURSE)
        side_stud_brick(s, f'exhaust-mount-{side}', '30414', FRAME, (0, 0, 1), (80 * sx, 230), COURSE)
        for i, z in enumerate((100, 180)):
            side_stud_brick(s, f'pod-panel-mount-{i}-{side}', '30414', HULL, face, (110 * sx, z), COURSE)
        s.box(f'pod-mid-{side}', '3008', FRAME, *xs(sx, 80, 100), 60, 220, COURSE)
        s.box(f'pod-in-{side}', '3007', HULL, *xs(sx, 40, 80), 60, 220, COURSE)
    for i, z in enumerate((-220, -140, -60)):
        s.box(f'core-{i}', '3001', FRAME, -20, 20, z, z + 80, COURSE)
    s.box('core-waist', '3010', HULL, -40, 40, 20, 40, COURSE)
    s.box('core-front', '3010', FRAME, -40, 40, 40, 60, COURSE)
    s.box('spine-s', '3007', FRAME, 0, 40, 60, 220, COURSE)
    s.box('spine-p', '3007', FRAME, -40, 0, 60, 220, COURSE)
    side_stud_brick(s, 'tail-mount', '30414', FRAME, (0, 0, 1), (0, 230), COURSE)

    s.step()  # Deck: tiles ahead of and behind the canopy, studded plates under it
    s.box('deck-bow', '87079', HULL, -40, 40, -220, -180, DECK)
    s.box('deck-bow-b', '2431', HULL, -40, 40, -180, -160, DECK)
    s.box('deck-bow-stripe', '2431', ACCENT, -40, 40, -160, -140, DECK)
    s.box('cockpit-floor', '3032', FRAME, -40, 40, -140, -20, DECK)
    s.box('cockpit-floor-aft', '3710', FRAME, -40, 40, -20, 0, DECK)
    s.box('deck-waist', '87079', HULL, -40, 40, 0, 40, DECK)

    s.step()  # Cockpit interior, seen through the canopy; the canopy keeps the four studs at x=+-10
    t = DECK - 8
    for side, sx in SIDES:
        s.box(f'cabin-sill-{side}', '3069b', PANEL, *xs(sx, 20, 40), -140, -100, t)
        s.box(f'cabin-side-{side}', '3069b', PANEL, *xs(sx, 20, 40), -80, -40, t)
    s.box('cabin-console', '2431', ACCENT, -40, 40, -100, -80, t)
    s.box('cabin-seat', '3068b', FRAME, -20, 20, -80, -40, t)
    s.box('cabin-aft', '87079', FRAME, -40, 40, -40, 0, t)

    s.step()  # Recessed spine between the pods: grille detail and twin swept tails on the outer columns
    s.box('spine-front', '87079', FRAME, -40, 40, 40, 80, DECK)
    s.box('spine-mid', '87079', FRAME, -40, 40, 80, 120, DECK)
    s.box('spine-grille-a', '2412b', PANEL, -20, 20, 120, 140, DECK)
    s.box('spine-grille-b', '2412b', PANEL, -20, 20, 140, 160, DECK)
    s.box('spine-aft', '87079', FRAME, -20, 20, 160, 240, DECK)
    for side, sx in SIDES:
        s.box(f'spine-edge-{side}', '3069b', FRAME, *xs(sx, 20, 40), 120, 160, DECK)
        s.add(f'tail-{side}', '2340', HULL, [30 * sx, COURSE - 72, 240], None, 'Swept tail on the spine edge')
        s.add(f'tail-cap-{side}', '3069b', ACCENT, [30 * sx, COURSE - 80, 240], Ry(90), 'Tail cap')

    s.step()  # Rounded pod tops: curved slopes back to back along each pod's centreline
    for side, sx in SIDES:
        for i, z in enumerate(range(40, 240, 40)):
            for half, (a, b), out in (('in', (40, 80), -1), ('out', (80, 120), 1)):
                x0, x1 = xs(sx, a, b)
                down = out * sx                        # +1: slope descends toward +X
                s.add(f'pod-top-{side}-{half}{i}', '15068', PANEL if i == 4 else HULL, [(x0 + x1) / 2, COURSE, z + 20],
                      Ry(-90 * down), 'Curved pod top')
    return s


def k2_k4(s, name, y):
    """K2/K4: forward core plates, then eight-stud bridges across the core/pod seams at x=+-40."""
    s.box(f'{name}-fwd', '3035' if y == K4 else '3032', FRAME, -40, 40, NOSE_STEP[y], -40, y)
    s.box(f'{name}-mid', '3032', FRAME, -40, 40, -40, 80, y)
    for side, sx in SIDES:
        s.box(f'{name}-pod-in-{side}', '3022', FRAME, *xs(sx, 40, 80), 40, 80, y)
    s.box(f'{name}-bridge', '3036', FRAME, -80, 80, 80, 200, y)
    s.box(f'{name}-bridge-tail', '3034', FRAME, -80, 80, 200, 240, y)


def flank(side):
    """SNOT side panel: authored upright in its own frame, then turned so local up faces outboard.

    Local X runs aft along the hull and local Y=0 is the hull's side-stud base plane. The upper
    tile row is local Z=+10 on starboard and -10 on port: the two proper rotations send local Z
    to opposite world directions. The parts are identical; only their arrangement differs.
    """
    s = Section(f'halcyon-flank-{side}.ldr', f'Halcyon {"starboard" if side == "s" else "port"} flank panel, '
                'built flat and mounted on side studs')
    upper = 10 if side == 's' else -10
    s.step()
    s.add('base-fwd', '3034', HULL, [-40, -8, 0], None, 'Two-row base plate on the side studs')
    s.add('base-aft', '3020', HULL, [80, -8, 0], None, 'Two-row base plate on the side studs')
    s.step()
    # The stripe's 1 x 8 tile spans the base-plate seam at local X=40, bonding the two plates.
    s.add('stripe-fwd', '2431', ACCENT, [-80, -16, upper], None, 'Accent stripe, level with the pod stripes')
    s.add('stripe-aft', '4162', ACCENT, [40, -16, upper], None, 'Accent stripe bridging the base-plate seam')
    s.add('lower-fwd', '4162', HULL, [-40, -16, -upper], None, 'Lower tile row')
    s.add('lower-aft', '2431', HULL, [80, -16, -upper], None, 'Lower tile row')
    return s


FLANK_R = {'s': orient(up=(1, 0, 0), along=(0, 0, 1)), 'p': orient(up=(-1, 0, 0), along=(0, 0, 1))}
FWD_R = orient(up=(0, 0, -1), along=(1, 0, 0))      # local up points forward
AFT_R = orient(up=(0, 0, 1), along=(1, 0, 0))       # local up points aft


def nozzle():
    """Exhaust built upright along its own axis; the root turns local up to face aft (+Z)."""
    s = Section('halcyon-exhaust.ldr', 'Halcyon exhaust nozzle: round plate, jumper, dish bell and glowing core')
    s.step()
    s.add('ring', '60474', FRAME, [0, 0, 0], None, 'Round 4 x 4 base seated on four aft-facing studs')
    s.step()
    s.add('jumper', '87580', FRAME, [0, -8, 0], None, 'Centre stud for the dish')
    s.step()
    s.add('bell', '3960', PANEL, [0, -24, 0], None, 'Nozzle bell')
    s.step()
    s.add('core', '4740', GLOW, [0, -32, 0], None, 'Glowing core')
    return s


def intake():
    """Intake ring and spinner, built upright along its own axis; the root turns it to face forward."""
    s = Section('halcyon-intake.ldr', 'Halcyon engine intake: round ring and truncated-cone spinner')
    s.step()
    s.add('ring', '60474', FRAME, [0, 0, 0], None, 'Round 4 x 4 intake ring on four forward-facing studs')
    s.step()
    s.add('hub', '3941', PANEL, [0, -24, 0], None, 'Spinner hub')
    s.step()
    s.add('spinner', '98100', HULL, [0, -48, 0], None, 'Spinner cone')
    return s


def nose():
    """Pointed nose in the ship frame: handed wedge-plate pairs under a triple-curved wedge.

    Each keel layer's pair fills the 80 LDU ahead of that layer's hull plates, so each step
    back overlaps the first hull row of the next layer up. The lower layers stop short of the
    tip, giving a chin that rises toward it.
    """
    s = Section('halcyon-nose.ldr', 'Halcyon nose: stepped handed wedge plates under a triple-curved wedge')
    for i, y in enumerate((K1, K2, K3, K4, K5)):
        s.step()
        zc = NOSE_STEP[y] - 40
        colour = HULL
        s.add(f'wedge-{i + 1}s', '41770', colour, [20, y, zc], None, 'Starboard half of the pointed plate')
        s.add(f'wedge-{i + 1}p', '41769', colour, [-20, y, zc], None, 'Port half of the pointed plate')
    s.step()
    s.add('cap', '47753', HULL, [0, K5 - 24, NOSE_STEP[K5] - 40], None, 'Triple-curved nose wedge')
    return s


def aft_cap():
    """Centre panel between the nozzles, built upright and turned to face aft."""
    s = Section('halcyon-aft-cap.ldr', 'Halcyon aft cap: dark panel with grille and two glowing vents')
    s.step()
    s.add('panel', '3020', FRAME, [0, 0, 0], None, 'Seated on the aft-facing tail studs')
    s.step()
    s.add('vent-s', '98138', GLOW, [30, -8, -10], None, 'Glowing vent')
    s.add('vent-p', '98138', GLOW, [-30, -8, -10], None, 'Glowing vent')
    s.add('grille', '2412b', PANEL, [0, -8, -10], None, 'Grille')
    s.add('lower', '2431', PANEL, [0, -8, 10], None, 'Lower tile')
    return s


def wing(side):
    """Swept wing: a handed 6 x 12 wing plate on a root splice that runs under the pod, fully tiled."""
    sx = 1 if side == 's' else -1
    s = Section(f'halcyon-wing-{side}.ldr', f'Halcyon {"starboard" if side == "s" else "port"} wing, root splice and tiles')
    s.step()
    s.box('splice', '3030', FRAME, *xs(sx, 80, 160), 40, 240, K2)
    s.step()
    s.add('wing', '30355' if side == 's' else '30356', HULL, [180 * sx, K3, 120], None, 'Handed 6 x 12 wing plate')
    s.step()

- **Technic skeleton:** it is built on `3703`/`3701` Technic bricks held with `4459` pins. That gives a long, slim, engineered-looking spine instead of a slab.
- **Real wing pairs:** it layers several `41769a`/`41770a` and `43722`/`43723` wings in dark grey and black. The result is a thin, swept, stepped silhouette.
- **Strong shape contrast:** it has a curved mudguard nose, an inverted triple-curved wedge at the rear, and dishes with round plates as thrusters. Colour changes are sparse, so the shape does most of the work.
- **Colour:** black and dark bluish grey, with only a couple of yellow accents.

## Redesign: "Kestrel Mk II"
This is a new silhouette, not a re-skin of Halcyon. It is a long, narrow arrowhead about 700 × 560 × 140 LDU.

1. **Silhouette**
   - A long, low nose that curves up into the canopy, using a mudguard or curved wedge.
   - Two layered wing pairs that sweep back, with the front pair shorter and the rear pair longer. Their tips are thin and angled.
   - Twin tail fins.
   - A cluster of three or four dish thrusters at the rear with trans-blue cores.
2. **Palette**
   - Dark bluish grey is dominant and black is the second colour, for panel breaks and the underside.
   - Yellow is limited to a few small accents: intake studs, one stripe per wing and cannon rings. That is roughly a quarter of the current amount.

3. **Construction**
   - **Core:** a Technic brick spine pinned with `4459`, with plate layers above and below.
   - **Side-stud course:** a `30414` course whose studs face ±X, forward and aft.
   - **Skins:** SNOT modules for the flanks, nacelle stripes, intakes, thruster cluster and wing-root cannons. Each is built upright in its own section and seated on a stud face using `stud − R·socket`.

I'll write a new generator, `output/kestrel4/generate.py`, with no Halcyon hull. It reuses only the helper functions (`orient`, `seat`, `Section`). The design is the Naganata's:
- **Layered frame:** build the ship from stacked, interleaved layers around a Technic core, as the Naganata does.
- **Stepped silhouette:** use many small plates and wings to make a stepped outline.
- **Visible detail:** put the detail on the surface, so it can be seen.

Before writing any code I'll do the following:
1. Read the rest of the Naganata MPD (offset 6000 onward).
2. Count its parts by type and layer, and list its sideways attachments and Technic holes and pins.
3. Write `kestrel4/brief.md` with a target of 450–600 parts.
4. Record the Jev check in `NOTES.md`. If Jev is unavailable, I'll use the FTS search.

## Design
Same concept, a bold yellow-striped dark grey and black fighter, about 720 LDU long. This time it has more structure.

1. **Exposed Technic spine**
   - Pinned `3703`/`3701` bricks, with `4459` pins and visible holes.
   - The top is open between the cockpit and the engines, so the Technic frame is part of the look.
   - A bare-core render checks the frame.
2. **Sideways skins**
   - Rows of `30414` and `87087` side-stud bricks carry hull panels.
   - Panels are built upright, then rotated onto each face.
   - Rows of `3665a` inverted slopes, `48336` handle plates and `3024` plates add surface relief and mounting points.
3. **Layered wings**
   - Per side: two or three stacked pairs of `41769a`/`41770a`, plus `43722a`/`43723a`.
   - Each layer is offset in height, length and sweep.
   - Tiles cover the studs, and the leading edges are yellow.
4. **Nose**
   - A curved `50745` mudguard over stepped wedge plates.
   - An inverted `43713` under the chin.
   - Slopes taper it into the canopy.
5. **Cockpit**
   - A `30384` canopy over an interior with a seat, console and side panels.
6. **Engines**
   - Twin or triple nacelles built from `3062b` round bricks, `2654a` dishes and `4073` plates.
   - Trans-blue cores.
   - Raised shrouds, intakes and grilles.
7. **Tail and surface detail**
   - Tall twin fins.
   - Wing-root cannons.
   - Antenna pins.
   - Vent grilles.
   - Round-plate rivet rows.
   - Handle plates as greebles.
   - Yellow cut tiles.
8. **Underside and stand**
   - The underside is plated and tiled, with a Technic belly pod.
   - A slim stand attaches through the spine.

## Process
1. Inspect any new parts' origins and connectors with `./ldraw-agent part`, and don't guess axes.
2. Build and review in modules: spine, nose, cockpit, wings, nacelles, tail and underside.
3. Run `review --contacts all` on each module and then on the whole ship, with all seven views.
4. Open **every** preview, plus a bare-core view and wing-root close-ups.
5. Check that:
   - the thumbnail silhouette is distinct,
   - no studs are left exposed,
   - the disconnected-group count is explained or fixed,
   - the Naganata's detail level is matched.
6. Revise until it holds up, then publish. In the report I'll give the part count, checks and limitations, and the images I opened.

## Questions
- Is a target of 450–600 parts fine, or do you want even more?
- Should I keep the stand, or use a floating pose?

code = r'''

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers
SP_TOP = ytop(4)             # top of the brick course on layers 2-4 (y = -40)
NAC_TOP = ytop(7)            # top of the nacelle brick course on layers 5-7 (y = -64)
FACE_YAW = {(0, 0, -1): 0, (1, 0, 0): -90, (0, 0, 1): 180, (-1, 0, 0): 90}


def side_stud(sec, id, colour, face, cx, cz, top, purpose=None):
    """30414 with its four side studs facing `face`; (cx, cz) is the brick centre in LDU."""
    return sec.add(id, '30414', colour, [cx, top, cz], Ry(FACE_YAW[tuple(face)]), purpose or f'side studs face {face}')


def deck_colour(cx, z):
    if cx in (-1, 0) and 7 <= z <= 17:
        return BK
    if cx in (-3, 2) and -8 <= z <= 6:
        return YL
    if cx in (-4, 3) and z >= 8:
        return BK
    return DG


def body():
    s = Section('kestrel4-body.ldr', 'Hull: Technic spine, wall bricks, side-stud mounts, deck, cockpit floor and interior')
    rng = random.Random(21)
    s.step()
    for k in range(6):
        z0 = -8 + 4 * k
        zc = (z0 + 2) * 20
        for cx in (-1, 0):
            s.add(f'spine-{k}-{cx}', '3701', BK, [cx * 20 + 10, SP_TOP, zc], Ry(90), 'Technic spine brick, holes across the hull')
        for dz in (-20, 0, 20):
            col = YL if WIN[0] <= z0 <= WIN[1] else BK
            s.add(f'pin-{k}-{dz}', '4459', col, [0, SP_TOP + 10, zc + dz], None, 'Friction pin locking the spine pair')
    s.step()
    reserved = set()
    for cx0, face in ((3, (1, 0, 0)), (-4, (-1, 0, 0))):
        for z0 in (-8, -4):
            side_stud(s, f'flank-mount-{cx0}-{z0}', DG, face, cx0 * 20 + 10, (z0 + 2) * 20, SP_TOP, 'Flank panel mount')
            reserved |= {(cx0, z) for z in range(z0, z0 + 4)}
    for cx0 in (-4, 0):
        side_stud(s, f'aft-mount-{cx0}', DG, (0, 0, 1), (cx0 + 2) * 20, 17 * 20 + 10, SP_TOP, 'Aft cap mount')
        reserved |= {(cx0 + i, 17) for i in range(4)}
    walls = {}
    for z in range(-8, 18):
        for cx in range(-4, 4):
            if cx in (-1, 0) and z <= 15:
                continue
            if cx not in (-1, 0) and WIN[0] <= z <= WIN[1]:
                continue
            if (cx, z) in reserved:
                continue
            walls[(cx, z)] = DG
    pack(s, walls, BRICK, SP_TOP, rng, 'z', maxlen=6, p2=0.3, prefix='wall', purpose='Wall brick course')
    s.step()
    deck = {(cx, z): DG for (cx, z) in FUS if z >= -8}
    pack(s, deck, PLATE, ytop(5), rng, 'z', maxlen=8, p2=0.35, prefix='deck', purpose='Deck plate layer')
    s.step()
    tiles = {(cx, z): deck_colour(cx, z) for (cx, z) in FUS
             if z >= -8 and not (-2 <= cx <= 1 and -7 <= z <= -1)}
    pack(s, tiles, TILE, ytop(6), rng, 'x', maxlen=4, p2=0.25, prefix='dt', purpose='Deck tile')
    t = ytop(6)
    for side, (a, b) in (('s', (1, 2)), ('p', (-2, -1))):
        s.rect('3069b', LG, a, b, -7, -5, t, 'sill', 'Cabin sill')
        s.rect('3069b', LG, a, b, -4, -2, t, 'side', 'Cabin side')
    s.rect('2431', YL, -2, 2, -5, -4, t, 'console', 'Instrument console')
    s.rect('3068b', BK, -1, 1, -4, -2, t, 'seat', 'Seat')
    s.rect('87079', BK, -2, 2, -2, 0, t, 'aft', 'Cabin aft')
    s.add('canopy', '30384', GLASS, [0, ytop(5), -90], None, 'Rounded canopy on the four floor studs')
    return s


def wing(side):
    sx = 1 if side == 's' else -1
    f = (lambda c: c) if sx == 1 else (lambda c: (-1 - c[0], c[1]))
    s = Section(f'kestrel4-wing-{side}.ldr', f'{side} wing: tiled top layer, yellow leading edge, cannon mount')
    rng = random.Random(31 if sx == 1 else 32)
    top = wing_cells(2)
    cannon = (9, 11)
    cells = {}
    for c in top:
        if c == cannon:
            continue
        lead = (c[0], c[1] - 1) not in top
        cells[f(c)] = YL if lead else BK if c[1] == 17 else DG
    s.step()
    pack(s, cells, TILE, ytop(2), rng, 'x', maxlen=4, p2=0.3, prefix='wt', purpose='Wing top tile')
    s.step()
    cx, z = f(cannon)
    s.rect('3024', DG, cx, cx + 1, z, z + 1, ytop(2), 'cm', 'Plate under cannon mount')
    s.step()
    s.add('cannon-mount', '87087', DG, [cx * 20 + 10, ytop(5), z * 20 + 10], None, 'Side stud faces forward for the cannon')
    return s


def nacelle(side):
    sx = 1 if side == 's' else -1
    f = (lambda c: c) if sx == 1 else (lambda c: (-1 - c[0], c[1]))
    s = Section(f'kestrel4-nacelle-{side}.ldr', f'{side} engine nacelle: plate base, brick course with side studs, tiles, fin')
    rng = random.Random(41 if sx == 1 else 42)
    for layer in (2, 3, 4):
        s.step()
        pack(s, {f(c): DG for c in NAC}, PLATE, ytop(layer), rng, 'x' if layer % 2 else 'z', maxlen=6, p2=0.3,
             prefix=f'np{layer}', purpose='Nacelle plate layer')
    s.step()
    bx = 120 * sx
    side_stud(s, 'front-mount', DG, (0, 0, -1), bx, 150, NAC_TOP, 'Intake mount')
    side_stud(s, 'rear-mount', DG, (0, 0, 1), bx, 350, NAC_TOP, 'Nozzle mount')
    for i, z0 in enumerate((9, 13)):
        side_stud(s, f'pod-mount-{i}', DG, (sx, 0, 0), 150 * sx, (z0 + 2) * 20, NAC_TOP, 'Outer panel mount')
    res = {(c[0], 7) for c in NAC} | {(c[0], 17) for c in NAC} | {(7, z) for z in range(9, 17)}
    cells = {f(c): DG for c in NAC if c not in res}
    pack(s, cells, BRICK, NAC_TOP, rng, 'z', maxlen=4, p2=0.3, prefix='nb', purpose='Nacelle brick course')
    s.step()
    fin = {(6, z) for z in range(10, 17)}
    tiles = {}
    for c in NAC:
        if c in fin:
            continue
        col = YL if c[0] in (5, 6) and 9 <= c[1] <= 15 else BK if c[1] >= 16 else DG
        tiles[f(c)] = col
    pack(s, tiles, TILE, ytop(8), rng, 'z', maxlen=4, p2=0.25, prefix='nt', purpose='Nacelle top tile')
    pack(s, {f(c): DG for c in fin}, PLATE, ytop(8), rng, 'z', maxlen=4, p2=0, prefix='fb', purpose='Fin base plate')
    for j in range(5):
        s.step()
        z0 = 10 + j
        base = 9 + 3 * j
        col = YL if j == 2 else DG
        pack(s, {f((6, z)): col for z in range(z0, 17)}, BRICK, ytop(base + 2), rng, 'z', maxlen=4, p2=0,
             prefix=f'fin{j}', purpose='Swept fin course')
        cx, z = f((6, z0))
        s.add(f'fin-slope-{j}', '54200', DG if j != 2 else YL, [cx * 20 + 10, ytop(base + 2), z * 20 + 10], None, 'Leading-edge slope')
    s.step()
    s.rect('63864', YL, *(lambda c: (c[0], c[0] + 1))(f((6, 14))), 14, 17, ytop(24), 'fcap', 'Fin cap')
    return s


FLANK_R = {'s': orient(up=(1, 0, 0), along=(0, 0, 1)), 'p': orient(up=(-1, 0, 0), along=(0, 0, 1))}
FWD_R = orient(up=(0, 0, -1), along=(1, 0, 0))
AFT_R = orient(up=(0, 0, 1), along=(1, 0, 0))


def flank(side):
    sx = 1 if side == 's' else -1
    s = Section(f'kestrel4-flank-{side}.ldr', f'{side} flank panel built flat and turned onto side studs')
    up = 10 * sx
    s.step().add('base', '3034', DG, [0, -8, 0], None, 'Two-row base plate on the side studs')
    s.step()
    s.add('stripe', '4162', YL, [0, -16, up], None, 'Yellow stripe')
    s.add('lower-a', '2431', BK, [-40, -16, -up], None, 'Lower tile')
    s.add('lower-b', '2431', DG, [40, -16, -up], None, 'Lower tile')
    return s


def pod_panel(side):
    s = Section(f'kestrel4-pod-panel-{side}.ldr', f'{side} nacelle outer stripe')
    s.step().add('base', '3460', DG, [0, -8, 0], None, 'One-row base on side studs')
    s.step().add('stripe', '4162', YL, [0, -16, 0], None, 'Stripe')
    return s


def intake():
    s = Section('kestrel4-intake.ldr', 'Intake ring, hub and spinner built along their own axis')
    s.step().add('ring', '60474', BK, [0, 0, 0], None, 'Round 4x4 on four forward studs')
    s.step().add('hub', '3941', DG, [0, -24, 0], None, 'Hub')
    s.step().add('spinner', '98100', YL, [0, -48, 0], None, 'Spinner')
    return s


def nozzle():
    s = Section('kestrel4-exhaust.ldr', 'Exhaust nozzle: ring, jumper, bell and glowing core')
    s.step().add('ring', '60474', BK, [0, 0, 0], None, 'Ring on four aft studs')
    s.step().add('jumper', '87580', BK, [0, -8, 0], None, 'Centre stud')
    s.step().add('bell', '3960', DG, [0, -24, 0], None, 'Bell')
    s.step().add('core', '4740', GLOW, [0, -32, 0], None, 'Glowing core')
    return s


def aft_cap():
    s = Section('kestrel4-aft-cap.ldr', 'Aft cap: dark panel with grille and glowing vents')
    s.step().add('panel', '3020', BK, [0, 0, 0], None, 'On aft-facing studs')
    s.step()
    s.add('vent-a', '98138', GLOW, [30, -8, -10], None, 'Vent')
    s.add('vent-b', '98138', GLOW, [-30, -8, -10], None, 'Vent')
    s.add('grille', '2412b', LG, [0, -8, -10], None, 'Grille')
    s.add('lower', '2431', DG, [0, -8, 10], None, 'Lower tile')
    return s


def cannon():
    s = Section('kestrel4-cannon.ldr', 'Wing-root cannon stacked along its own axis')
    for i, (ref, col, y) in enumerate((('85861', BK, 0), ('3062b', DG, -24), ('85861', YL, -32),
                                       ('3062b', DG, -56), ('98138', BK, -64))):
        s.step().add(f'barrel-{i}', ref, col, [0, y, 0])
    return s


def build():
    mods = [keel(), nose(), body(), wing('s'), wing('p'), nacelle('s'), nacelle('p'), flank('s'), flank('p'),
            pod_panel('s'), pod_panel('p'), intake(), nozzle(), aft_cap(), cannon()]
    root = Section('kestrel4.ldr', 'Kestrel Mk IV strike skiff, floating pose')
    for name in ('keel', 'nose', 'body'):
        root.step().add(name, f'kestrel4-{name}.ldr', 16, [0, 0, 0])
    root.step()
    for side in 'sp':
        root.add(f'wing-{side}', f'kestrel4-wing-{side}.ldr', 16, [0, 0, 0])
        root.add(f'nacelle-{side}', f'kestrel4-nacelle-{side}.ldr', 16, [0, 0, 0])
    root.step()
    for side, sx in (('s', 1), ('p', -1)):
        root.add(f'flank-{side}', f'kestrel4-flank-{side}.ldr', 16,
                 seat(FLANK_R[side], [-70, 0, 10 * sx], [80 * sx, SP_TOP + 10, -150]), FLANK_R[side])
        root.add(f'pod-panel-{side}', f'kestrel4-pod-panel-{side}.ldr', 16,
                 seat(FLANK_R[side], [-70, 0, 0], [160 * sx, NAC_TOP + 10, 190]), FLANK_R[side])
    root.step()
    for side, sx in (('s', 1), ('p', -1)):
        bx = 120 * sx
        root.add(f'intake-{side}', 'kestrel4-intake.ldr', 16, seat(FWD_R, [10, 8, 10], [bx + 10, NAC_TOP + 10, 140]), FWD_R)
        root.add(f'exhaust-{side}', 'kestrel4-exhaust.ldr', 16, seat(AFT_R, [10, 8, -10], [bx + 10, NAC_TOP + 10, 360]), AFT_R)
        root.add(f'cannon-{side}', 'kestrel4-cannon.ldr', 16, seat(FWD_R, [0, 8, 0], [190 * sx, ytop(5) + 10, 220]), FWD_R)
        root.add(f'aft-cap-{side}', 'kestrel4-aft-cap.ldr', 16,
                 seat(AFT_R, [10, 8, -10], [40 * sx + 10, SP_TOP + 10, 360]), AFT_R)
    return dict(version=1, author=AUTHOR, sections=[root.plan()] + [m.plan() for m in mods])


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument('--output', type=Path, default=HERE / 'kestrel4.plan.json')
    a = ap.parse_args()
    plan = build()
    a.output.write_text(json.dumps(plan, indent=1) + '\n')
    n = sum(len(st) for sec in plan['sections'] for st in sec['steps'])
    print(a.output, 'placements incl. module refs:', n)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
'''

# Flexible parts with LSynth

Use **lsynth-nova** to shape hoses, cables, strings, flexible axles, rubber bands and treads, or to lay out separate chain links. Keep the constraints as editable source, generate an MPD asset, then use the normal plan and review commands. The adapter uses the Python port's CLI; it does not implement another curve or belt solver.

For the rigid construction around those paths, start with the [26 annotated construction studies](../../lsynth-examples/README.md) and [industrial assembly lessons](technic-patterns/industrial-assemblies.md): track carriers, pneumatic controls, cable terminations and shaped frames. Their supplied synthesis scenes are visual references; the smaller examples below are easier starting inputs for generation.

## Install and try

Keep the `lsynth-nova` checkout beside this repository:

```sh
./setup.sh --with-lsynth
./ldraw-agent flex types
./ldraw-agent flex build examples/flex/hose.ldr --output output/flex/hose.mpd
./ldraw-agent review output/flex/hose.mpd --contacts none
```

Open the review's previews. [Small examples](../../examples/flex/README.md) cover a hose, a rubber band and a chain. Copy a constraint file into your own `output/` directory before editing it. `doctor` reports whether the optional package is installed. `LSYNTH_SOURCE=/path/to/lsynth-nova ./setup.sh --with-lsynth` accepts another checkout location. Ordinary setup and builds do not require LSynth; `uv sync` may remove this optional installation, so use the setup flag again afterward.

Only synthesis needs LSynth installed. Generated assets embed the required LSynth geometry and work with the ordinary LDraw library, including in LeoCAD. Do not run `lsynth --install-parts` for this workflow: the adapter leaves the parts library unchanged.

## Describe a path

A hose uses at least two visible constraints, in path order, inside an ordinary LDR or MPD:

```text
0 SYNTH BEGIN TECHNIC_PNEUMATIC_HOSE_BEVELED 4
1 4 -60 0 0 0 -1 0 1 0 0 0 0 1 LS01.dat
1 4 0 -40 0 0 -1 0 1 0 0 0 0 1 LS01.dat
1 4 60 0 0 0 -1 0 1 0 0 0 0 1 LS01.dat
0 SYNTH END
```

Coordinates are LDU. Each marker's local **−Y axis points along the path**: away from the start, into the end. These matrices point along +X. Move markers to route the hose, and rotate them to control its direction. Use enough clearance for the actual cross section, and inspect bends and endpoints after every change. `flex types` lists supported methods, product aliases and marker parts. Product aliases are hints, not proof that the resulting pose has the correct manufactured length.

A band uses actual pulley, wheel or gear placements as constraints, in loop order. Choose only parts listed under `band_constraints`; their configured radii determine the wrap. `0 SYNTH INSIDE`, `OUTSIDE` and `CROSS` control the route. Start with two separated, coplanar pulleys and inspect a simple loop before adding crossings. Put each wheel in the source once. Visible wheel constraints remain real placements in the generated asset; `SYNTH HIDE` suppresses them when the wheels already belong to another assembly.

Use explicit colours in each SYNTH BEGIN. Keep the original visible constraints even if using `SYNTH HIDE`: LSynth comments markers out in its output, which cannot reliably reconstruct the source on a later run. The adapter rejects already synthesized inputs. Multiple SYNTH blocks and ordinary MPD submodels are supported; blocks must stay within one FILE section. Keep source section names unique when importing several assets, or use the existing `extract --namespace` command to rename a dependency closure.

## Generate and reuse

```sh
./ldraw-agent flex build output/my-hose.ldr --output output/my-hose.mpd
# After changing the original constraints:
./ldraw-agent flex build output/my-hose.ldr --output output/my-hose.mpd --force
```

This writes the MPD and a `.manifest.json` with source/configuration hashes, engine version, source credits, embedded geometry provenance, each synthesized block and any recorded compatibility repairs. Unknown types, warnings from LSynth, empty synthesis and assembly validation errors fail without replacing an existing asset. `--timeout` bounds the subprocess. `--namespace` changes the generated part prefix; it defaults to the output filename stem. The source is never overwritten.

Import it through the existing plan format. Place the `root` returned by `flex build`:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "author": "Your name",
  "assets": ["my-hose.mpd"],
  "sections": [{
    "name": "main.ldr",
    "description": "Assembly containing a posed hose",
    "steps": [[{"id": "hose", "ref": "my-hose.ldr", "colour": 4, "at": [0, 0, 0]}]]
  }]
}
```

Asset paths are relative to the plan. Regenerate after moving endpoints relative to one another; a rigid placement only moves the completed pose. The generated colour remains explicit. Use the normal `build` and `review` commands for the complete assembly, and deliver the constraint source and manifest with it.

## What the checks mean

Continuous hoses, cables, bands and one-piece rubber treads become **one posed embedded part per block**. LSynth's stretched cross sections belong inside that part's geometry, and are not independent BOM items. Separate Technic chain/tread links and BRICK_ARC bricks stay ordinary rigid physical placements. Minifigure chains are supplied as a complete item and stay one posed part. Posed part IDs describe geometry; they are not an inventory or retail part-number claim.

The normal prohibition on stretching, shearing or mirroring complete parts remains in force. For generated rigid links only, the adapter can recover rounding from LSynth's four-decimal output when each corrected matrix coefficient differs by at most 0.00005. Every such repair is recorded. It never applies this repair to input placements or to stretched hose/band geometry. Larger defects fail validation.

Check every route's bend radius as well as its endpoints. Fixed-segment types such as `TECHNIC_RIBBED_HOSE` place separate rigid rings about 5.5 LDU apart, and those rings open visible gaps once neighbours turn more than about 7°. LSynth's stiff curves can also form near-hairpins when waypoints sit close together. Stretched types such as pneumatic hose stay continuous, but can still bend too tightly or cross another hose.

The [pneumatic press](../../examples/flex/pneumatic-press/README.md) places hose ends on the nozzle frames from each part's shadow data. Its test measures sleeve seating, minimum bend radius, tube-to-tube distance and part clearance; reuse those checks for new routes.

Start flex studies with `review --contacts none`. Bounds, source checks, previews and BOM comparison still run, but connectivity and material clearance are not established. Posed parts have no verified connector metadata, stock length, tension, minimum bend radius or elasticity.
